precise-hero.title: The Precise Hero
description: A short platformer where you control a hero suffering from narcolepsy. The game plays with the contradiction of being a precision platformer while making you lose control of your character at the worst possible moments.
Developed in 3 days for Todo Game Jam 2024. The theme was "out of control" and it placed 4th in the gameplay category.

contributions.title: Player controller
contributions.text: Precise, responsive movement is the backbone of the game, so the contradiction with the sleep mechanic hits just right. I put a lot of effort into perfecting the 'feel' of the character's controls.

contributions.title: Sleep mechanic
contributions.text: To make the most of the game's main gimmick, I designed a solid progression. Early on, falling asleep is a minor inconvenience; later it becomes a mechanic you must actively manage to advance.

contributions.title: Level design
contributions.text: To make the game speedrun-friendly and fully leverage the sleep mechanic, I designed levels that can be approached in multiple ways depending on the 'sleep cycle' you enter them with.

contributions.title: Aesthetics
contributions.text: We found a theme and setting that naturally supported the main mechanic, with an art style and sound design aligned with the concept.

point-of-no-return.title: Point of No Return
description: A game about exploration and planet colonisation where space itself expands over time. Some areas of the map are easier or harder to reach depending on when you arrive, as objects may start too close together. You gather resources, colonise planets and upgrade your ship to travel faster than the expansion of space.
Developed in 5 days for Unity Jam 2024 by Tooling.gg. The theme was "expanding" and it placed 2nd overall.

contributions.title: Scaling world
contributions.text: For the game's main mechanic I designed and programmed the system that constantly pushes every object apart, while keeping the world and its physics working as expected.

contributions.title: Map design
contributions.text: To reward exploration, points of interest are spread across the map. There is a preferred path, but the map is an open world where players can head in any direction at any time.

contributions.title: Upgrade system
contributions.text: I implemented a progression and upgrade system: you collect resources to gradually improve your ship and discover upgrades scattered throughout the map.

contributions.title: Player controller
contributions.text: I built a physics-based ship controller to sell the feeling of steering a propelled body through space, requiring careful handling and fuel management.

feather-fallout.title: Feather Fallout
description: A tower defense game where turrets can switch between two colours, each able to shoot only enemies of the matching colour. It adds a dynamic twist to the genre: you constantly re-tune your turrets based on which colour dominates the screen at any moment.
Developed in 2 weeks for 1-Bit Jam #4. The theme was "tower" and the limitation was that games could only show two colours on screen at any time.

contributions.title: Dynamic tower defense
contributions.text: I designed and programmed the core loop, where turrets flip between two colours and only damage matching enemies — turning colour management into the central tactical decision.

contributions.title: Paired turrets
contributions.text: Turrets work in colour pairs, so covering a lane means balancing both colours at once. I tuned their placement and switching rules to keep that trade-off constantly interesting.

contributions.title: In-game economy
contributions.text: I designed the round-based economy — DPS, effectiveness values and per-round budgets — so every purchase between waves is a meaningful decision.

contributions.title: Aesthetics
contributions.text: We committed to a strict two-colour palette and a matching setting and sound design, turning the jam's limitation into the game's identity.

giro.title: G!RO
giro.team: Made by the Negone collective — 2 programmers, 2 artists
description: A fast-paced arcade-hypercasual game where you pilot a constantly rotating spaceship using a single button. Timing your one input against the spin is everything — a simple control scheme with a deep, score-chasing skill ceiling.
Won the "Most Enjoyable Game" audience award at Fun&Serious Bilbao 2022, and was nominated for "Best Retro Game".

contributions.title: One-button control
contributions.text: As lead programmer and designer I built the core control scheme: the ship never stops rotating and a single button is your only input, so the whole game is about reading the spin and committing at the right instant.

contributions.title: Arcade feel & scoring
contributions.text: I designed the score-chasing loop and the game feel — combos, feedback and escalation — that made it click with the Fun&Serious audience and earn the Most Enjoyable Game award.
